failure_counters.detail: P-series round1 -> N-series round2 -> M-series round3 accepted; no identical-input retries counted (each round changed the artifact per verifier findings)

dispatcher binding exited 0 on the first run (134 assertions), then 136 after the review closed VB-1; no identical-input retry was needed. All defects found while BUILDING the check are itemised as mid_card_repairs, not as failures of a submitted artifact.
mid_card_repairs: journal writes wrapped in a SAVEPOINT after a failed watermark CAS could leave an orphan outbox row
event ids re-keyed to (session, sequence) after a cross-principal outbox.id collision
writer_client_id now moves together with writer_epoch on takeover
nested json_extract paths corrected (SQLite evaluates each path independently)
session.attach with request_write_owner routed through the write gate instead of the read handler
ACKNOWLEDGED/COMPLETED results rebuilt to the published PendingResult/ControlResult/AttachResult shapes
hand-written JSON Schema subset replaced by the repository jsonschema/v6 compiler (single validator)
checker defects fixed: sessionState destructure order, single-connection deadlock, nil map write, unguarded type assertion, PASS-with-zero-assertions hole
published RelativePath pattern neutralised only for that exact published text, semantics re-enforced, count pinned at 1
disclosed_incidents: first loopback HTTP connect failed once with a Windows dial timeout; transport-only retry (max 3) added and the retry count asserted
internal/domain/v24_sessions.go left gofmt-dirtied by a broad go fmt run; restored byte-exactly via git checkout and verified clean by two independent reviewers
round-1 verdict REJECT (verifier w1701_verifier): 1 blocker + 4 majors + 1 note, all reproduced by the executor's own mutation run before any reply was written

6 product-level defects, not merely test gaps: peer gate undecisional on the serve path, decorative reply grading, ASCII-only leak scan, self-fulfilling read-only assertion, client-named workspace registration, superseded credentials left live
no branch was delayed and no failure counter was reset; the card was reworked in place and re-reviewed by a different identity
round-1 verdict REJECT (qoder-desktop:/root/w0401_verifier): 1 blocker + 4 majors + minors, each reproduced by the executor before replying
two genuine product defects: an authorized workspace reference was transferable across principals, and the local inventory claimed absence over unexamined ground

one integration defect with blast radius beyond this card: registering test.context under the v2.4 pointer shadowed accepted fixture bindings (W17-C02, W12-C13, C01/C02/C13); repaired by default-forwarding plus the legacy tool environment
the first receipt contained claims stronger than their evidence (identical-content dedupe, three vs four gofmt-dirty files, pre-delivery binding invocations); corrected in the reworked receipt
no branch was delayed and no failure counter was reset; the card remains unaccepted until a fresh verdict

round-2 verdict REJECT: a NEW blocker the first review and the executor both missed - this card is the first writer of WorkspaceBinding/BootstrapStage/BootstrapReplay/Project rows into domain_versions, none of which exists in the frozen domain schema, and the accepted RestoreBackup path validates every kind unconditionally, so release recovery becomes RESTORE_CONTRACT_INCOMPATIBLE. The chosen storage design is the defect, not a test gap.

major: command-id replay is not scoped to the workspace reference, so a reused id can return a different directory's project binding; two principals over one canonical directory still yield three Project rows
major: the round-1 per-file import-failure persistence finding was NOT actually fixed; two mutations show it (N10/N11)

refuted claims in the executor receipt: the C13 tool_env justification (resources.py has a hard-coded fallback, so C13 passes without it), the forwarding-only regression argument (a bare non-forwarding build answers legacy selectors with PASS 136, i.e. the shadowing test was under-specified), a retained pre-delivery 121/123 sentence, contradictory gofmt-dirty lists, and a retracted dedupe claim still present in reuse_notes

the refreshed receipt pinned internal/domain/v24_sessions.go at the hash of the scope-violating gofmt-mangled content (it was regenerated before the restore), so artifact_hash_check fails 1 of 22 while the tree itself is clean

selector-scope regressions: --task-id W04 alone and --task-id W06 alone now answer with this card's construction check (136) where the legacy registry answered 20 or failed; task_id-only invocations must not resolve to a card check
no branch was delayed and no failure counter reset; the card stays unaccepted
required_before_next_review: replace the domain_versions writes for the four non-schema kinds with a storage path the accepted backup/restore contract tolerates (or hand the durable record to the owning card with a migration), and prove RestoreBackup still round-trips
scope command-id replay by workspace reference, and make the same directory over two principals resolve to one project identity deliberately or refuse
actually persist per-file import failures durably, not only in the in-memory scan result
regenerate the receipt after any file change so no artifact hash points at mangled content, and remove the retained false sentences
restore exact legacy behaviour for task_id-only invocations of test.context

disclosed_incidents: round-2 REJECT found a recovery-breaking blocker (non-schema kinds in domain_versions) that round 1 and the executor both missed; storage narrowed to domain_objects and the check now re-validates every version row the way restore does
the round-1 scanner blocker was only partly closed then; depth/entry/link/\.git forms are now gated and each has its own assertion and mutation
two further product majors (cross-principal binding reuse; unscoped command-id replay) and the registry shadowing of task-only invocations were fixed
several receipt claims were stronger than their evidence and have been corrected, including an artifact hash pinned to scope-violating content, which the executor self-reported separately
no branch was delayed and no counter reset; the card is still unaccepted
required_before_acceptance: a verifier identity that has not reviewed this card must re-run the binding (152 assertions), the three mutation suites, the neighbour regressions and the selector parity table on this state

disclosed_incidents: round-3 REJECT was confined to W04-01-EVIDENCE: the receipt carried stale sentences from earlier rounds and one overclaim, because it had been patched forward three times instead of regenerated

the same review confirmed by direct experiment that the recovery blocker found in round 2 is genuinely closed: a real CreateBackup/RestoreBackup of a bootstrapped database restores, and injecting a WorkspaceBinding row into domain_versions reproduces the failure
the read path that had been described as probed without being probed is now asserted (SEC-FOREIGN-BINDING-NOT-READABLE, SEC-OWNING-PRINCIPAL-STILL-READS-ITS-BINDING)
the surviving-mutation list is now complete, with a stated reason per entry, and the fourth round of mutations (U1-U6, T6b) was run to establish it
no branch delayed and no counter reset; the card remains unaccepted
required_before_acceptance: a fourth verifier identity must reproduce the 154-assertion state, the binding invocation, the parity table, the neighbour regressions and the mutation list, and must rule on whether the interim domain_objects placement is acceptable until the migration owner takes it over

disclosed_incidents: rounds 3 and 4 rejected on the evidence file rather than the product: stale counts, an obsolete invocation claim, an invented OUTPUT/NEGATIVE phase mapping, a wrong gofmt-dirty count, under-reported parity failures, and an assertion that could not fail

the same round-4 review named two real coverage gaps (durable per-file failure list, measurement mode) which are now asserted, and both assertions were proved to be able to fail by V1 and V2 in the current matrix
both reviews confirmed independently that the recovery blocker from round 2 is closed, by running a real CreateBackup/RestoreBackup round-trip

round 5 then found two more defects in its own evidence: the receipt cited a mutation runner that no longer exists on disk, and two carried-forward cases turned out to break compilation instead of reaching an assertion. The whole matrix is now one re-runnable file, the lost runner is disclosed rather than cited, and T2b/T3b carry the two properties onto named assertions
eight cases whose anchors the accepted fixes rewrote are reported ANCHOR_MISSING, each naming the current case that now tests the same property, instead of being dropped from the count
the delivered check_report.json and regression_log.txt were regenerated from the current state; a stale 152-assertion check report had been hashed into the previous receipt
receipt generation is now self-verifying: it parses the dispatch log and refuses to publish if a pinned value disagrees with the captured evidence
no branch delayed, no counter reset; the card is still unaccepted
required_before_acceptance: a fifth verifier identity must reproduce the current state and rule on the interim storage placement

disclosed_incidents: rounds 1-4 each rejected this card: two on product defects, two on its own evidence text; the fifth identity reproduced the current state, re-ran the whole matrix without a single flip, ran 17 mutations of its own, and performed its own backup/restore round-trip before accepting
no counter was reset and no branch was deferred on the way here; the card stayed EXECUTION_REPORTED until an identity that had not reviewed it before ruled

W01-G03 rerun preconditions
L1 re-point package.validate_v24 at merge

VB-4 (W03-02 review): v2 writer attribution uses the envelope client_id against client_sessions.writer_client_id, not the authenticated OS principal; bind it in the handoff/native-bootstrap card before any multi-principal or LIVE claim
VB-2 (W03-02 review): internal/domain legacy tests require RESEARCHOS_GO pointing at the locked go.exe; it is not a registered required_env, so a full suite run without it shows 20+ false failures
v2 writer-lease TTL defaults to 15m via RESEARCHOS_WRITER_LEASE_TTL (mirrors the existing credential TTL ceiling); the real lease policy must be qualified before any LIVE handoff case

internal/api embeds byte-identical copies of the two pinned schemas and verifies sha256 at startup; if the spec package re-issues either schema, both copies and the pinned hashes must move together in the owner card

W17-01 disclosed gaps: credential-import and workspace-choose withdrawal closures are not exercised because no reachable input makes those replies nonconformant; only the bootstrap result def pins a violable value

W17-01 disclosed gap: proving the DEFAULT peer lookup is a real OS query (not a constant) needs a second interactive OS account; carried to W17-99 for formal cases A10/A11/C02/C22 as a resource requirement

W17-01 disclosed gap: internal/host revokes only the credential issued in the same host directory; enforcing one owner instance per principal belongs to the card that owns host startup and instance locking
W17-01 follow-up: apps/cli and apps/control are not yet rewired onto internal/host; the bridge exists and is qualified but the product binaries still use their own credential path
VB-4 stays open and is now actionable: internal/host holds a verified OS principal, so writer attribution can be bound to it instead of trusting the envelope client_id

out-of-scope gofmt debt from accepted cards: internal/api/v2.go, internal/domain/client_protocol_schema.go and internal/domain/v24_sessions.go are gofmt-dirty and were left byte-identical by W17-01; the owning card must format them with its own evidence
W04-01 acceptance is pending: a verifier identity that has not reviewed this card must re-run the binding (136 assertions), the 25 mutations and the three neighbour regressions on the reworked state

W04-01 registered test.context in execution/v2.4/commands.json rev 10 for check_id W04-01 and forwards every other selector to ops/ci/context.py with the legacy tool environment; W06-G02 was never implemented by that harness and fails identically under --spec v2.0

W04-01 obligation: workspace.register and project.bootstrap are still NOT_IMPLEMENTED over /v2/command because internal/domain/client_protocol.go is outside this card's write scope; the owning card must route them and re-qualify

W04-01 obligation: internal/host still passes a nil chooser over the pipe, so no real Desktop directory dialog or CLI init path exists; until it does a user cannot actually choose a directory in the product

W04-01 scope incident (self-reported): a directory-wide gofmt -w rewrote two accepted files outside the card scope; restored byte-for-byte and recorded in integrity_events. The next card must format named files only.

W04-01 blocker (round-2 review): the card writes four non-schema entity kinds into domain_versions, which breaks the accepted RestoreBackup recovery contract. No further W04 card may start until this is re-architected and recovery is re-proven.

R5-F1 (W04-01 round-5 review): most typed refusals still pin only the code substring, not Fault.Status: access escalation POLICY_DENIED, foreign-binding read/revoke/list/bootstrap FORBIDDEN, replay COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT, PATH_OUT_OF_SCOPE and WORKSPACE_REVOKED can move HTTP status unnoticed. The receipt's status-pinning claim covers exactly the two branches it names, so this is not a false claim - it is unfinished hardening.

R5-F2 (W04-01 round-5 review): five defence-in-depth branches have no fixture: directoryHeldByOther's second condition, the UNC branch, the unknown-status guard, the file-failure absolute-path guard and the continuation alive-check. Either add a hostile-adapter fixture or keep them disclosed the way U4/U5 are.
R5-F3 (W04-01 round-5 review): immaterial: receipt.check_results.failures prints [] where the program emits null.

R5-F4 (W04-01 round-5 review): review_request_round5.json lists MG17 among surviving cases, but MG17 is not a row in the 53-case current matrix; the prose should not name cases the matrix does not contain.
